stem: Hepatitis C is described as which kind of process affecting the liver?

options.label: A
options.text: Liver inflammation and damage caused by autoimmune attack on hepatocytes
options.misconception: Confuses viral hepatitis with autoimmune hepatitis.
options.explanation: Autoimmune hepatitis is inflammation from an immune attack on the body's own hepatocytes; hepatitis C is caused by a virus.

options.label: B
options.text: Liver inflammation and damage caused by chronic heavy alcohol use
options.misconception: Confuses viral hepatitis with alcoholic hepatitis.
options.explanation: Alcoholic hepatitis results from heavy alcohol use; hepatitis C is an infection with a virus, not a toxic effect of ethanol.

options.label: C
options.text: Liver inflammation and damage caused by a toxic drug reaction
options.misconception: Confuses viral hepatitis with drug-induced liver injury.
options.explanation: Drug-induced hepatitis, such as from acetaminophen or isoniazid, is a toxic reaction; hepatitis C is a viral infection.

options.label: D
options.text: Liver inflammation and damage caused by a viral infection
options.misconception: None — hepatitis C is a viral infection causing liver inflammation and damage.
options.explanation: NIDDK defines hepatitis C as a viral infection that causes liver inflammation and damage.

options.label: E
options.text: Liver inflammation and damage caused by reduced hepatic blood flow
options.misconception: Confuses viral hepatitis with ischemic hepatitis (shock liver).
options.explanation: Ischemic hepatitis follows reduced hepatic blood flow, as in shock or heart failure; hepatitis C is an infectious, viral process.

context: Learning objective: Hepatitis C is a viral infection that causes liver inflammation and damage.
